transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Um, well, I guess I'm here because... I just feel really wound up lately. Pretty much all day. It's like my body is just... bracing for something to happen. Even when I'm just sitting at my computer for work, or, you know, trying to relax after dinner. It just doesn't stop.
Do you find yourself worrying a lot about different things in your life, like work, relationships, or other everyday issues?

Yeah, I suppose I do. It's just... my mind doesn't really settle. It sort of jumps around. I'll think about my sister down in Arecibo, and then I'm worrying if I messed something up at work, or if my husband is okay driving home. And then there's church stuff, and bills. Just... always thinking about what could go wrong before it even does.
Have you noticed any physical symptoms along with this feeling of being wound up, like restlessness, muscle tension, or trouble sleeping?

Um... I suppose my sleep isn't great. I mean, I do fall asleep eventually most nights. But... I tend to wake up around three or four in the morning. Just thinking about things... like my sister's next appointment, or some server issue at work. And... I don't know, even when I get enough hours in, I just start the morning feeling like I never really rested.
Do you feel like your worrying is something you can't really control, like it takes over even when you're trying to focus on something else?

I suppose so, yes. Um... I'll try to stop. I'll tell myself, 'Daniela, enough, focus on this report.' But... it doesn't really work. One small thought just turns into five more. And... before I know it, I've spent half an hour just checking messages or... replaying what could go wrong. It just sort of happens.
Do you ever feel sudden episodes of intense fear or discomfort, like your heart is racing, you can't breathe, or you feel like something terrible is going to happen right then?
Um... no. Not really. I don't get those sudden... feelings like you're saying. My heart doesn't race or anything. It's mostly just... the thinking.
Do you find that you feel tired or lacking in energy, even if you're not doing much physically?
Um... I don't think so. I mean, I feel tired because of the sleep thing, but... not just out of nowhere, I guess. Mostly I just feel normal tired.
Do you find yourself getting more irritable or easily annoyed lately, even over small things?

Um... I suppose a little. I try to be patient, usually. But... just small things lately. Like if there's a late update in a documentation meeting at work... or someone singing off-tempo at choir. Or just... if I'm cooking on Sunday and get asked too many questions. I guess I've been answering a bit sharper than I mean to.
Do you find it hard to concentrate on things, like work tasks or reading, because your mind keeps wandering or you're preoccupied with worries?
Um... no, I don't think so. I can focus fine. At work, I just... I do my job, look at the screen, and it's fine. My mind doesn't really wander off like that.
Do you have trouble falling asleep at night, even when you're physically tired?

Um... falling asleep is usually fine. I do fall asleep eventually. But... I tend to wake up around three or four in the morning. Just thinking about things... like my sister's next appointment, or some server issue at work. And... I don't know, even if I manage to get enough hours in, I just start the morning feeling like I never really rested.
Do you notice any physical symptoms like muscle tension or restlessness along with your anxiety?

Um... I suppose so. That's... actually kind of why I made the appointment. I just feel... wound up, I guess. Most of the day. Like my body is just... bracing for something. Even when I'm just sitting at my computer, or... or trying to relax after dinner. It's just... there.
How long have you been feeling this way, with your mind constantly worrying and your body feeling wound up?
Um... I suppose it's been... about thirteen months. That's when... well, my sister down in Arecibo started needing a lot more help from the family. So... since around then, I guess.
Do you feel that your anxiety about things is out of proportion to the actual situation, or do you feel like you can't stop worrying even when there's nothing specific to worry about?

Um... I suppose it's just hard to turn off. My mind just kind of... goes from one thing to another. 

Like my sister, obviously. But then... I'll start worrying about whether I missed something at the office, or... my husband driving home. Then it's church commitments, or... the bills. It just doesn't stop. I always find myself... preparing for problems that haven't even happened yet. So... yes, I guess.
